quotes.race: Weatherbys Digital Solutions Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Into Battle is such a good-looking horse and his work has been decent, but I wasn't expecting that. I expect the handicapper will take a dim view, but I'm sure there's plenty more to come - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He slightly disappointed us after the London Gold Cup last season but he's a massive horse and has done well through the winter. I hope he'll be progressive in handicaps from 1m to 1m2f this season. He looks to start the year on a fair mark. 16-04-25

runners.comment: Eventually swallowed up last time; style of racing aside, has leading chance on best form
runners.spotlight: Allowed too much rope in winning his sole bumper attempt but was eventually swallowed up, having again established a clear lead, in latest hurdles start (1m7f); style of racing aside, holds a leading chance on peak figures; this track seems likely to suit.

runners.comment: Gradually heading in the right direction over hurdles; clear second at Catterick latest
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who is gradually heading in the right direction over hurdles, as form figures of 532 demonstrate; beaten only 1l by the market leader, pair clear, at Catterick (1m7f) most recently; his turn under rules looks near.

runners.breeder: S A S Haras Le Gue

stable_tour.quote: He's been running on the Flat in France to a good level. He's a lovely, robust, athletic horse who seems to have taken really nicely to hurdling at home. quotes.race: Oliver Jorg Ties Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Fountains Blenhein was pricking his ears and dossing but you half want them to doss as, when push comes to shove, they save plenty. We got done for a bit of toe [early in the straight] but his stamina started to kick in at three out and the further I was going the better I was getting - Gavin Sheehan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Twice-raced 5yo who is likely to build on Huntingdon win and improve further
runners.spotlight: Twice-raced 5yo who is a half-brother to two useful winners for his connections; lacked fluency but took a big step forward to win at Huntingdon (2m), shaping as if he'll stay further; respected with further progress likely.

runners.comment: Disappointing over C&D last time but may rebound; has solid form otherwise
runners.spotlight: Disappointing favourite over C&D last time, folding rather tamely once headed, but record suggests a rebound is plausible; has solid form otherwise and proved game, as opposed to tame, in gaining his Cheltenham win.

quotes.race: Enquire About The Cheltenham Bloodstock Club Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were a bit disappointed to get beat first time at Warwick but the winner [Moneygarrow] was rated 128 and had experience. We thought the track would suit Step Ahead and he's loved the ground - Mat Nicholls, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had three starts for us, and in two of them he has been beaten by Dan Skelton's Moneygarrow. We were beaten five lengths by him in an Ascot bumper last Christmas when Don Cantillon trained our horse, and it was a similar distance at Warwick last time out on his hurdles debut. We were pleased with him. He didn't jump as we hoped he might, but he's got a huge stride - the biggest of any in the yard - and maybe the hurdles just got in the way a bit. He'll probably run in a maiden hurdle somewhere between Christmas and the new year, and it'll be chasing next year when you see the best of him. 24-12-25

runners.comment: 0-5 in Irish points; not a particularly promising type
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-5 in Irish points, good third in May 2025 the final time; subsequently sold for £22,500; not a particularly promising type, as rules newcomers go; the market may offer further guidance.

runners.comment: Pedigree suggests he'll improve for the step up in trip on hurdles debut
runners.spotlight: Has shown a bit of ability in point/rules bumpers; only a modest third of four at Fontwell most recently but pedigree suggests he'll be suited by this step up in distance and switch to hurdles.

racecards.verdict: It may be worth keeping the faith in STEP AHEAD. The other main contenders are  Caspari and Fountains Blenhein.

quotes.race: Conferencing And Events At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap (A Jockey Club Grassroots Mile Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I had no plan. Rukaana was a little bit slow away but he's still learning but when the penny dropped he quickened nicely. He should get plenty of confidence from coming through them like that and he's hit the line strongly. He's a big horse but coming here onto good ground suited him and I'd be confident he'd get a mile and a quarter - Christian Howarth, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Boost Your Acca With BetMGM Nursery Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Rukaana is a big lad and, once I got the position I wanted to be in, I was hoping I could set sail early enough because I think he'll stay further. He showed a nice attitude going to the line.  - Ben Curtis, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He came from Charlie Hills on the Flat and will be going juvenile hurdling this season. He's got a really nice attitude to jumping and hopefully he can pick up a couple of nice juvenile races. 06-11-24

runners.spotlight: Got better with each start in Irish points but his rules form isn't convincing, beaten long way on handicap debut (2m5f) most recently; needs improvement back down in distance.

runners.comment: Similar type to Largy Panic and has something to prove
runners.spotlight: Showed promise in Irish points but looks far from solid on rules form, well beaten on handicap debut (2m) most recently; similar type to Largy Panic and has something to prove.

stable_tour.quote: He was runner-up in a point-to-point in Ireland in the spring and ran well first time out for us at Plumpton last month when he probably just needed the run. We're going to duck and dive with him as I don't think he wants deep winter ground. He ran at Newbury on Friday and finished down the field behind Act Of Innocence, but I really think he's going to be one for the spring. 03-12-25

racecards.verdict: This second run after wind surgery may be the time to catch KOTARI. Second choice is Rukaana.

runners.spotlight: Gained both chase wins three years ago; dropped 8lb since last run and looks attractively treated on best form but is returning from 16-month layoff; the betting may offer further guidance.

runners.comment: Perhaps needed latest run; good chance if tapping back into earlier progress
runners.spotlight: Perhaps needed the run in C&D event nine days ago on return from break; largely productive over hurdles/fences otherwise this term, winning five times; good chance if tapping back into that progress.

quotes.race: Chailey Classic & Vintage Tractor Club Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: They went far too fast in front and the race just fell apart, so I doubt the form will stand up. Freddie did ride a really nice race, though. Jorebel has been a fantastic horse and owes us nothing. He's great to train and very straightforward - Chris Gordon, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Clever BetGoodwin Conditional Jockeys' Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I'm so sorry about that. I looked behind me and all I could see was a loose horse [Graham], and the one behind me [Hill Station] was covered by that loose horse. I looked at the screen and realised there was another one next to me. Coming to the line it was sickening because there was a big delay and I didn't know if I'd won or not. For a horse, it's good for them to have a nice time rather than being slapped down the shoulder and given a push. For Jorebel's sake, I was trying to give him a nice time because I thought I was so far ahead, but I wasn't - Freddie Gordon, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: We've had a great time with him, winning four races since September. I think because our horses weren't in great form last season, they're all quite well handicapped. He has been very tough a few times - once when Freddie thought he'd won quite cosily and eased down and another horse came to get him. Jorebel did very well to pick up and just win it. He had a real good scrap at Worcester when he came out on top and another at Lingfield last time on his first run over fences. It wasn't the strongest race and hopefully the handicapper won't be too silly about it. He pulled clear with another horse who had very little form. It's down to the handicapper really whether he can win another one. He looked at the end of his tether the other day, but naturally you'd like to see him find more improvement with more experience of jumping. 01-12-25

runners.comment: This second run since wind surgery may be the time to catch him; Sean Bowen booked
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-8 over rules fences but form is largely consistent and this second run since wind surgery may be the time to catch him, especially with Sean Bowen up for first time; interesting today.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Tingle Creek Festival Sale Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Southoftheborder will be a proper horse, we've only taken half of the wraps off him. It's nice because we've got a lot of good novices coming out at the moment. Willmount looked extra-special the other day, even Jingko Blue and Jango Baie.  You wouldn't want to overdo this fella because he's very big and you could wind him up too much. We've gone very gently with him. Nico said he was lovely and he could have gone around again.   I should think the Listed race here on Tingle Creek weekend could be the sort of thing we'd look at, but he'd want to go gently. He will get further when we want to. Derek O'Connor told us to buy him. Willmount could head to the race that was the Kennel Gate. Nicky Henderson, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He won his first three races [a point, a bumper and a maiden hurdle] before he was twice a beaten favourite. All his racing has been around two miles, but I'd be pretty sure he'll stay further than that in time and he'll almost certainly make a chaser on top of that. He's summered very well and is ready to go as soon as the ground is safe for him. 22-10-24

runners.comment: Productive over hurdles; ran encouragingly in latest chase start; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Productive spell over hurdles culminated in a hat-trick last spring; 0-4 switched to fences since but ran encouragingly at Chepstow most recently; clear possibilities off a reduced mark.

quotes.race: Harry & Betty Savill Memorial Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Friend Sean has been brilliant this season. It's taken him a long time to get into this rhythm of winning, there's just been a load of maturity and he's gotten a lot better with time. I was wide on the home turn but that didn't bother me too much, it gave me a bit of space and he ran a cracker. He travelled and jumped and did everything right. We don't know his ceiling, as we didn't think he was well-handicapped six months ago but he's won four times since  - Cameron Iles, rider.

runners.comment: Generally progressive and has a good strike-rate for current yard; still of interest
runners.spotlight: Generally progressive and has a good strike-rate for current yard; absent since an excusable effort (bled from nose) four months ago; seemingly saved for spring ground and remains of interest.

quotes.race: Position Payout At bet365 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Pep Talking is absolutely amazing, he loves good ground. He bounced off it in front - Billy Aprahamian, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Southwell Golf Club Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Pep Talking has been a fantastic horse for us and has become a bit of a handicapper's nightmare as he only just does enough. He loves his jumping and hopefully has more to come next season. That will be him for this campaign - Billy Aprahamian, trainer.

racecards.verdict: There are factors that may well enable SOUTHOFTHEBORDER to take advantage of a reduced mark. My Friend Sean is second pick.

racecards.race_name: Virgin Bet Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Solid performances in notable handicaps this season; respected back down in class
runners.spotlight: Solid performances in notable handicaps this season, winning the Badger Beers at Wincanton then fourth in the Stayers' Veterans' Final at Sandown and Ladbrokes Trophy over C&D; retains plenty of ability despite his advancing years; respected back down in class.

quotes.race: 64th Badger Beers Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gustavian was overdue it. He had his pants pulled down at Exeter when he ran another stormer. Sam [Twiston-Davies] was so livid, but we couldn't resist having another one in that veterans' race and Credo came through and beat him that day. He had a really good second in the fog at Aintree and he literally got nailed that day. He obviously does go on a bit of decent ground and it does help his jumping. I think physically early season he probably just used his back a bit more and felt good in his body as he used it a bit more. Watching him jump today you don't see any horse jump that sort of trip bar Desert Orchid. He was awesome. I suppose the wind operation has been significant to some degree, but he has run well in this race before and maybe that is all he had to do the way the race was. He is a bit one paced and you are a bit limited on dropping in him really. It is easier to dictate everything under your own steam. He is a 10-year-old, but you would think he was a five-year-old as he wants to go and you never have to chivvy him along he just goes. He is a good horse to make the running with as he does travel out of the gate. It has become an important race, but we never thought about it like that until we won it, and then when we won it, we thought we would come back again and we will keep coming back for as many as we can - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

quotes.race: BetVictor Super Boost Has Arrived Veterans' Handicap Chase (Leg 2 Of The Stayers' Veterans' Series)
quotes.quote: Gustavian made blunders down the back and although he makes them, he doesn't often blunder himself out of it, but he did today - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I might be really boring and run him straight in the Veterans' Final. It might feel like a long way away, but it's just after Christmas and that's coming fast. He had a harder race than some might think at Wincanton; he was a bit wobbly afterwards and cranky the next day. He's perfect now, but I'm not in a hurry to do anything with him because he'll never give himself an easy race. He runs well fresh, so we'll go to the Veterans' Final and then hopefully the Ladbrokes Trophy at Kempton, which we won with Forward Plan last year. It's right before Cheltenham so doesn't get many runners, but is worth more than the Ultima - that's the sort of race we'd love to run him in. 23-11-25

This season will be the toughest because we don't have the safety blanket of novice events. He proved he doesn't need a bog at Exeter in February and his jumping, although he fell last time, is good nine times out of ten. We hope he can click in a good three-mile handicap chase. 12-10-23

runners.comment: Folded tamely last time but could have more to offer provided he's back on song
runners.spotlight: Contrasting performances since switched to handicap chases, winning narrowly at Sandown then folding tamely at Ascot, both over 3m; presents a dilemma but could have more to offer provided he's back on song and it's too soon to write him off.

quotes.race: Howden Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Welcom To Cartries is a beautiful horse. A lot of those good ones I've got at the minute don't tend to do anything quickly ? look at Stay Away Fay this time last year - but he gallops all day and something like the River Don (Novice Hurdle at Doncaster on January 27] might suit him. I have no doubt he'll make a similar model to Stay Away Fay, not now but as a chaser next year. When he fills into his frame and jumps a fence next season that will be the making of him - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'm at a loss to explain his disappointing return at Cheltenham last month. His jumping was a bit lethargic and he was beaten some way out. We've since done all the usual tests but nothing has come to light. I had quite high hopes for him this season, but after that performance it's back to the drawing board. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Scored at Ludlow in most recent completed start; remains well treated on peak form
runners.spotlight: Mid-race faller in the Stayers' Veterans' Final at Sandown last time; ended a long losing spell with his Ludlow performance in most recent completed start and he remains well treated on historical data, which includes a useful win over this C&D.

quotes.race: Commodore Cup Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I think we were a shade lucky with Annsam, but he's been with us a long time and we've had so many good days with him. He had an injury to his hock a few years ago and that stopped him going on properly, but it's always nice when those old boys get their heads in front - Evan Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Racing Club Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Annsam is a smashing old boy on his day. If you're being brutal about it, this ground is hard work and I'd say it stopped a lot of them behind us. I wouldn't get carried away but he's a horse who wins races wherever you go - winning trainer Evan Williams.

quotes.race: Howden Silver Cup Handicap Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were only going on breeding and what we were half hoping Annsam could do. I have to admit I was a bit critical of the handicapper after his victory at Ludlow. I thought we had just tootled around in a small-field race. I have to admit he was right - Evan Williams, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'm told Tom Segal, Pricewise of the Racing Post, is fond of him and Tom knows things before I even think about them! I'd like to get a run under Annsam's belt quietly to blow the cobwebs away as he's a big, raw, strong horse. He's in a race at Ascot on Saturday but I'm not in love with going there. That said, he'll need a run because if he's too fresh he can be very, very bullish. He lost all chance when making a terrible early mistake in the old Racing Post Chase [Coral Trophy] last season but that was because I'd left him too fresh. He could be a horse, if he progresses, for the Coral Gold Cup or Grand National. He's lovely, still young and raw, but with a bit of luck I wouldn't rule out those good races. He's definitely got the ability. 26-10-22

Two weeks ago he had a bad fall in the veterans' chase at Sandown won by Nocte Volatus. Up to then he'd been jumping well and is normally a beautiful jumper. Before that he won at Ludlow, a track that suits him perfectly because it was his third win there. He'll need a confidence booster now at a minor track, quite possibly Ludlow. He can handle it soft but doesn't want it too deep. 14-01-26

runners.comment: For a couple of reasons he has more to prove than the other 11yos in this field
runners.spotlight: Has more to prove than the other 11yos in this field, with form this season suggesting that age may be catching up with him and virtually all of his chase outings at 2m4f; it remains to be seen whether this longer trip sparks a resurgence.

quotes.race: Coming Soon BioWaveGO International Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Es Perfecto was very keen last time and the combination of going up in trip and slower pace didn't help us, but he still ran very well. It was a weak enough affair today, but it was good to get his head in front and he settled well. Hopefully it will help his confidence and he'll be chasing next season, but I wouldn't be sure about plans for the rest of the season - Tom Bellamy, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He didn't win in his first season over fences but ran some really solid races and bumped into some good horses. He'll go down the handicap route, from two and a half to three miles, and should win. 25-10-24

He should win chases this season. He didn't win in his first season over fences but he ran some really solid races and bumped into some good horses. He'll go down the handicap route, from 2m4f to 3m. 07-11-24

runners.owner: J Hinds, A Head & G L Moore
runners.comment: Back in much better form at Plumpton the last twice; may progress further over fences
runners.spotlight: Back in much better form with a success and creditable second at Plumpton (3m1f) in last two starts; still has low mileage over fences and may be capable of further progress; upped in grade but receives plenty of weight all round; possibilities.

stable_tour.quote: He's honest and could end up running in three-mile chases this season. He's been mainly running over shorter, but he looks like a staying chaser and that's the way he's heading. 28-10-25

runners.spotlight: Winner of sole French start then ran well at Ascot but that promise was in 2022; sold for £20,000 last May; market instructive on return from mammoth absence.

runners.comment: Two wins last year at about 2m; ran well over 2m4f last time; may remain competitive
runners.spotlight: Gained his spring/autumn wins last year at about 2m; ran well over 2m4f at Plumpton most recently; may remain competitive, back down in distance.

quotes.race: Grace And Dotty Country Clothing Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was a good performance. Huntingdon was a bit quick for He's A Latchico last time and we thought a stiffer track on slower ground would suit him better. He's a three-time winner round Fontwell and won on the Flat at Sandown, which tells you he enjoys a test. He showed speed on the Flat when he was younger, so it wasn't a surprise he travelled so well. Tom [Queally, jockey] had a practice on him before at Huntingdon and he was good on him today -  Josh Moore, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: The step up in trip has helped He's A Latchico he hits a flat spot but stayed on well in the straight when I got a nice split - Rhys Clutterbuck, jockey.

runners.comment: Has shown improvement in handicaps, winning easily at Ludlow then fourth over C&D
runners.spotlight: Has taken his form to a new level since switched to handicaps, winning easily at Ludlow (2m) then fourth over C&D; may do better still; enters calculations.

runners.comment: Has lost his form since running well on reappearance; opposed
runners.spotlight: Has lost his form since running well on reappearance and a return to Huntingdon made no difference last time (2-2 there previously); opposed.

runners.comment: May still be up to winning races, having found only one rival too good last time
runners.spotlight: Veteran who may still be up to winning races, having found only one rival too good at Fakenham (2m) last time; fighting chance off same mark.

quotes.race: Visit racingtv.com Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Takeit Easy was too keen and it was a messy old race - they didn't go quick enough and I probably ended up riding him too handy. He's a good horse, he ran well the last day but there was too much traffic in the way. It wouldn't have done him harm and he probably learnt loads from it which is why he won here. There's no reason why he can't go again, he handles that ground well - Kielan Woods, jockey.

runners.breeder: A Blin, Mme A Blin, Et Al
runners.comment: Competitively treated on belated return to hurdles; on last winning chase mark
runners.spotlight: Hasn't raced over hurdles for nearly three years but is competitively treated assuming he's in top form; on last winning chase mark.

runners.owner: G C Stevens And Mrs C Fry

prev_owners.owner: Gary Stevens And Manhole Covers Limited

runners.comment: Handicap form is in better races; may take advantage of reduced mark back down in grade
runners.spotlight: Gained sole hurdles success in a weak maiden but his handicap form is in Class 2 and Class 3; may take advantage of a reduced mark dropped back in grade.

quotes.race: 888Sport What's Your Thinking Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: "High Fibre is a nice horse. He didn't get a race at York and he got in a tangle and stopped in his run. I had him in the valuable nursery here ten days ago but he came out as he had a rash and I had to back off him. I felt like it was a good spot and it was a competitive enough race" - Ralph Beckett, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We had high hopes for him as a juvenile but we had to wait and ended up thinking it would be best if he avoided losing his novice status cheaply, so he ran on the Flat but picked up an injury. He's back in work now and I hope he'll be out over Christmas. He had some good Flat form and could be a useful novice hurdler. 04-10-23

runners.comment: Drops back in grade and returns to the scene of his hurdles debut win; interesting
runners.spotlight: Dual Flat winner whose form in juvenile hurdles comprises an emphatic success over C&D and non-completions (pulled up both times) in Grade 2 races; interesting back down in class and returned to Kempton, with progress under this code still possible.

quotes.race: Live Racing Streaming At CopyBet Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: From the first day we schooled Sonic Pioneer he took to it amazingly well. For a three-year-old with that size and scope, he could jump a fence. He was a strong stayer on the Flat and seems to go on any ground. It was very impressive. You don't want to get too carried away, although it's quite hard not to, because there are a few nice horses in the division. But the way he's won, maybe he could be a Triumph hurdler -  trainer Martin Keighley, speaking on Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He's come from Jack Morland and has some very good form on the Flat. He stays well. He won impressively at Beverley over 1m2f on soft ground and then pulled away from the rest when second over 1m4f at Pontefract. With juvenile hurdlers, they must be strong stayers and go with cut in the ground, and he ticks those boxes. We've been doing plenty of schooling with him and I really like him. I think he could be above average and I'm looking forward to him running. 12-11-25

prev_owners.owner: P Inglett, S De Zoete And C Milln

runners.comment: Perhaps isn't quite ready to strike, having gained last five wins in the month of May
runners.spotlight: Somewhat resurgent last time and is on a handy mark but perhaps isn't quite ready to strike, having gained last five wins (Flat/hurdles) in the month of May.

racecards.verdict: Back in calmer waters, SONIC PIONEER (nap) is well worth another chance. High Fibre is second choice.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 He's A Latchico, 9/2 Sonic Pioneer, 5/1 Takeit Easy,  High Fibre, 7/1 Poet Laureate,  Wild Goose,  Time Interval, 14/1 Flamelco, 16/1 Diyaken

racecards.race_name: Virgin Bet Open Hunters' Chase

runners.comment: Listed winner in his prime and has made a solid start to hunter chasing
runners.spotlight: Listed winner in his prime and has made a solid start to hunter chasing, namely a close second and easy success at Wincanton; should follow up.

quotes.race: bet365 Premier Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We'll probably run Thunder Rock in the Bowl at Aintree, a flat three miles will suit. We'll take him there fresh. He'll have to improve again but he'll have a little each-way chance - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Colin Parker Memorial Intermediate Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I missed three out but on the whole Thunder Rock's jumping was very good and the minute I gave him a squeeze from the back of three out I was back on it. I never really had a moment's worry. I wouldn't see any issue with fences and that is definitely his trip for now - Sean Bowen, jockey.

quotes.race: Racing Welfare Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thunder Rock was good. He's progressed through from his bumper. He was very good at Uttoxeter and I thought the step up in trip would suit. I wasn't surprised to see him win like that. He's going to be rated in the late 140s or maybe early 150s so we're not far off Graded company. There's a graded race back here in a month's time so that will probably be the plan and he could be good. He's always threatened to be and will only improve. I don't know where the ceiling is with him yet - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Quiz Clothing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It wasn't Thunder Rock's track at Sandown last time, he was keen and he did too much. I was a bit nervous running him back quick today and I was really happy with him. He'll be a lovely chaser next season, he has a bright future - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: M1 Agency Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought Thunder Rock was a silly price as it was a decent race. The plan is to go to the EBF Final at Sandown - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Dransfields CIU Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thunder Rock won nicely - he travelled well and jumped well. He'll be seen to better effect on softer ground but he's done nothing wrong yet - Adrian Heskin, jockey.

quotes.race: Get Daily Tips At racingtv.com Intermediate Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wanted to go wide with Thunder Rock, but I'd have preferred a bit more cover. He was quite keen again and that was a good performance. He's quite a nice horse and I'd say that's a good bumper. - Adrian Heskin, rider

stable_tour.quote: I never really got him 100 per cent last season. He had a fibrillating heart when he ran at Ascot and I didn't have the same horse after that. A good break seems to have done him the world of good, and he's dropped down the handicap. If he gets his mojo back, he could be very well handicapped. He's another one for veterans' chases after Christmas. 23-10-25

He'll start off in the Colin Parker Memorial Chase on Sunday. The form of his Ayr run at the end of last season worked out well, with Unexpected Party winning recently at Chepstow. We'll start out over fences and, while we'll be aiming at Graded races, he's not the biggest or scopiest, so I wouldn't be afraid to go back over hurdles if chasing doesn't suit. 01-11-23

runners.comment: Somewhat resurgent last time but doesn't look the force of old
runners.spotlight: Unconvincing record for current yard; somewhat resurgent at Catterick last time but that effort is well short of his fairly useful best form.

stable_tour.quote: He's back in. We might look at the Aintree Foxhunters' with him if we can get him qualified in time. It's not guaranteed but a possibility. He ran well around Market Rasen and his form is good. He should make his presence felt in races like the Summer Plate. 06-03-24

racecards.verdict: Based on peak form and indeed recent evidence, THUNDER ROCK should comfortably beat his sole rival.
racecards.betting_forecast: 1/10 Thunder Rock, 13/2 Fix At All

racecards.race_name: Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Military Amateur Jockeys Handicap Hurdle (Sponsored By Team Forces)

runners.owner: Jb Harper And Cavalry And Guards
runners.comment: Better known as a chaser but ran well when back over hurdles last month; eased in grade
runners.spotlight: Better known as a chaser now but was third in a better race than this when reverting to hurdles at Warwick (2m, heavy; also suited by good) last month, and subsequent 32l defeat over fences came in a good-quality contest; must be considered.

quotes.race: P.J. Foley Memorial Flat Race
quotes.quote: He's a big weak horse and maybe one for next year - Gordon Elliott, trainer of Homme D'Un Soir.

stable_tour.quote: He won his bumper at Gowran Park but got beaten next time in a messy six-runner bumper at Leopardstown. He's jumping very well and we're looking forward to getting him out soon. 09-11-20

prev_owners.owner: Darren Cahill & J R Brennan & E Hughes & Kiva Cromwell

runners.comment: Didn't run badly at Taunton a fortnight ago but needs to build on that effort here
runners.spotlight: Won two juvenile hurdles for Anthony Charlton last season but largely disappointing in handicaps for new stable this term, albeit not running badly when fifth at Taunton (2m, good) this month; needs to up his game.

runners.breeder: Sarl Igep Haras Du Chateau De Rabodanges

quotes.race: Racing Excellence Conditional Jockeys' Training Series Handicap Hurdle (Part Of The RE Series)
quotes.quote: Thankyouandplease didn't come off the bridle. I've always thought a lot of him but it didn't go his way at Plumpton. He's in the zone at home, so we got him back out quickly, and we'll do the same again as he can go off 95 at Exeter next Thursday. He's in at Taunton [on Thursday] and it's tempting, but the ground would be too quick for him. Logically, a bit of time to Exeter should help and he can go in again hopefully. We've been knocking on the door, hopefully we're hitting a purple patch now and he can add to it next week - Syd Hosie, trainer.

runners.comment: C&D winner; behind Thankyouplease here this month but can turn the tables today
runners.spotlight: Good-ground C&D winner in November, despite racing a bit too freely; just over 19l behind Thankyouandplease over C&D this month but his margin of defeat was magnified by a last-flight jumping error and the good to soft ground probably wasn't ideal for him; he has a nice pull in the weights today and the services of top military rider Jody Sole.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Wincanton in November and then ran well when second in a three-horse military hurdle race at Wincanton the next time. He probably should have won that day. He's being aimed at the military hurdle race at Sandown on February 6, and then a similar race at the Grand Military meeting on the Friday before Cheltenham. He got stuck in the mud at Wincanton last week - we wouldn't run if the ground was soft or heavy again as he definitely didn't enjoy that. He's heading for those military races because his owner Kate Kenyon's husband is an ex-military man. There's three nice hurdle races there, two at Sandown and one at Wincanton later on in the year, and those would be his targets for the spring. 21-01-26

runners.comment: Went close off basement Flat mark this month but others have more compelling claims
runners.spotlight: Best of three hurdle runs for new stable this season when second of five in soft-ground Leicester seller (2m4f) in December; reverts to this code after going close off his basement Flat mark three weeks ago but others have more compelling claims; first ride under rules for Elizabeth Feakes.

quotes.race: Knocknarea Opportunity Claiming Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bigz Belief seems to enjoy it out in front and letting him dictate. He jumped brilliant and galloped all the way to the line - James Smith, rider

quotes.race: Join The Business Club At Naas Racecourse Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bigz Belief toughed it out well when they came to him. I expected him to run well. He came on from his last start when running a cracker at Punchestown. Sam said that when he went into pop hurdles he made mistakes, when he saw a horse he needed to make his mind up for him, and I thought when they came to him he'd be caught. Thankfully he pulled it out all the way to the line. We'll look for something similar next - Matthew Smith, trainer

quotes.race: Racing Again On 27th May Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Bigz Belief did it well and got a lovely run around, I was able to control it wherever I went. When I got stuck into him up the straight he picked up well. The ground was a little worry as I thought he might have needed a cut, but he was fourth in his maiden on good ground. He won over two miles on heavy ground over hurdles and seems top enjoy it out in front - Dylan Browne McMonagle, rider.

quotes.race: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bigz Belief got a grand ride, I told him to go out in front. We were a bit worried about the ground. His jumping was a lot better today - Matt Smith, trainer.

racecards.verdict: Topweight HOMME D'UN SOIR is now 5lb lower than when placed in a stronger hurdle race than this two starts ago and gets the nod.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Thankyouandplease, 3/1 Homme d'Un Soir, 5/1 Western Soldier, 6/1 Bigz Belief, 7/1 Moutarde

racecards.race_name: Cheese & Cider Raceday April 1st Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners.breeder: G Cherel, Mme I Pacault et al
runners.comment: Third behind two next-time-out winners at Taunton last month, after layoff; same mark here
runners.spotlight: No longer the force of old but returned from 342-day absence with a pretty good third at Taunton (3m, good to soft) last month behind two next-time-out winners and competes off the same mark here; respected.

quotes.race: Motor Auction Group Novices' Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jatiluwih jinked at a puddle on the way down and I went out the side door. He's a really nice horse and he did well to give that weight to some nice horses - David Maxwell, rider.

quotes.race: Shropshire Homes Novices' Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jatiluwih was found for me in France by Guy Petit, who assured me  he was a nice horse even though his form over there is nothing to write home about, The horse gave me a great feel and has won well so that is a good omen for his future - David Maxwell, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He's quite a nice horse and I expect he'll go back hunter chasing at some point. We'll be looking at handicaps before then. 25-10-21

prev_owners.owner: Mrs R Treacy & Mrs T J Kidd

runners.comment: Two wins this season (2m3f/2m4f); on tough mark for first attempt at 3m, though
runners.spotlight: In career-best form this season, winning here (2m4f, good) and at Taunton (2m3f, heavy); well beaten on latest outing, though, and remains on tough mark for first 3m attempt under rules.

runners.owner: The Galloping Dentist At 45 The Green
runners.comment: Good-ground winner last summer; makes stable debut after layoff; market may guide
runners.spotlight: Dual point winner who came good under rules for Max Comley at Worcester (2m7f, good; first-time visor) last summer; absent since a lesser effort the following month and goes without a visor here but still worth a glance in the betting on this stable debut.

runners.owner: S Clare G Kennington & C Knowles

prev_owners.owner: S Clare G Kennington C Knowles & J Reed
I & C Gosden, M Sharp & G Kennington

quotes.race: Kenn Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Striking A Pose is rated 130 so he was supposed to win like that. He's a nice chap and a gorgeous-looking horse and it was nice to watch all the way round - his ears were pricked and he didn't put a foot wrong. I think 2m4f is perfect, he's got a bit of class about him so he's not short of speed. I'm sure he'll end up over 3m but this trip is fine on genuine soft ground. I don't think we'll step him up to three this season. We've got some options now, he's qualified for the EBF Final at Sandown in a couple of weeks. He's probably not an Albert Bartlett horse but he might be competitive at Sandown, or he could go to Aintree. I expect we'll lean to Sandown. He'll be a lovely chaser for next season - Joe Tizzard, assistant to trainer Colin Tizzard.

quotes.race: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing "National Hunt" Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Striking A Pose has learnt his job over two miles and the form from Ascot looked quite nice. He's a point-to-point winner so stepping him up in trip worked a treat. He's a gorgeous-looking four-year-old and is a nice horse who's at the right end of the handicap who we hope will continue progressing through the ranks. He'll go over fences next season and he won't run again until the new year. - Joe Tizzard, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: He just seems to love it at Exeter. We could back over fences soon but he was third the other day and that was a good run, so we'll probably pick and choose with him. The handicapper has had his say with him though. 07-11-24

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Du Saubouas
runners.comment: Launched handicap career with two soft-ground wins this year; open to further improvement
runners.spotlight: Launched handicap career with two soft-ground wins over 3m2f this year (one under Freddie Robson); fell when last in action and needs to prove he's fully effective on good ground but could still have significant further improvement to come.

runners.owner: Harry Fry Racing Syndicate Miss Goldfire
runners.comment: Ended 2025 with some below-par efforts but she won twice on good ground last spring
runners.spotlight: Dual winner on good ground last spring (2m5f/2m7f); returned from break with three lesser efforts in the autumn and has been off for another three months since but she's back on a good mark.

stable_tour.quote: She won on her debut at Wetherby and showed a really good attitude. She could run in the Listed mares' bumper at Cheltenham in November as she's only four and she'd have to run under a penalty in a normal bumper. We could look at all those black-type bumpers this season and I'm not in a hurry to go over hurdles with her. She seems to have progressed over the summer. 04-10-23

runners.comment: Good-ground winner who was second here (2m5f, heavy) last month; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who won a good-ground Ffos Las maiden (2m) in the autumn and has finished second in two heavy-ground handicaps this year, the latter over 2m5f here; there's a good chance this new trip-and-ground combination will also suit, so he goes on the shortlist.

runners.comment: Seemingly back in good nick when close fourth over C&D this month; a possible
runners.spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner who seemed to have been refreshed by a 12-week break when a very respectable fourth over C&D (good to soft) in refitted cheekpieces this month; in the mix if in similar form.

quotes.race: Racing TV Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: The step up in trip has suited Jack Sprat who is still a bit of a baby. I had a target two out when I chased the leader and hit the front at the right time as he may have pricked his ears if he was in front too long. The ground on the stands rail was less churned up and he enjoyed it - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's one of those consistent handicappers who always wins his races. It didn't quite happen for him over fences last year, but he appreciated going back over hurdles when a good second at Bangor. 05-11-25
Yet to win, but he made the frame in a bumper and has been placed over hurdles. He has been backward but is improving and, consequently, could be well handicapped to get off the mark. 28-09-23

runners.comment: Form of penultimate run worked out well; considered on first attempt at a staying trip
runners.spotlight: Remote when third at Newbury (2m4f, soft) last month and remains winless since 2023; however, the form of his keeping-on fourth at Taunton (2m3f, good) two starts ago has worked out well and he's too well handicapped to be ruled out on this first attempt at a staying trip.

quotes.race: Champion Hats Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's taken a while for the penny to drop. Balboa has had two runs but he still had a look at the first (hurdle). We got a bit of good fortune with the non-runners but that's racing and you've got to kick the ball when it's in front of you. He's ok and he's solid, he seems to handle the soft ground. We might turn up at the Cheltenham meeting in November, although we do have some higher rated who could go there. Milton Harris, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's a winner waiting to happen. He's fairly typical, in that he had a good juvenile season and then probably paid for that a little bit as he was a little overrated when he started last season. He ran very respectably at Taunton the other day when a good fourth in a close finish. He's in at Doncaster on Friday and I would envisage him running well over 2m4f or 3m this spring and getting his head in front at some stage again. 21-01-26

runners.comment: Well held on last month's stable debut when may yet stage a revival for Olly Murphy
runners.spotlight: Largely out of form for an Irish stable last year and ought to have coped better with the soft ground when well-held fourth behind Mr Griffiths on last month's stable debut at Warwick (3m2f); sports refitted cheekpieces today, though, and may yet stage a revival for Olly Murphy.

racecards.verdict: Runner-up on both outings this year, AT THE OCHE is probably still on a good mark for this first attempt at 3m.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Mr Griffiths, 3/1 At The Oche, 6/1 Jatiluwih, 9/1 Kells Priory, 10/1 Striking A Pose,  Jack Sprat, 12/1 Miss Goldfire,  Balboa, 16/1 Our Dylan,  Jullou De Grissay

racecards.race_name: Molson Coors "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Pulled up when 400-1 for recent rules debut at Exeter (2m)
runners.spotlight: Pulled up when 400-1 for recent rules debut at Exeter (2m, good to soft).

runners.owner: M-A Middleton, J Perry, K Phillips
runners.comment: Showed clear promise in first two of three bumpers; considered each-way on hurdle debut
runners.spotlight: Not far behind Kilnew Supreme when fourth in good-ground bumper here in November and also showed clear promise when fifth of 15 at Exeter (soft) the following month; safely held in good-quality Kempton bumper last month but still considered each-way on hurdle debut.

runners.comment: Irish point winner; flopped badly on rules debut but ought to be capable of much better
runners.spotlight: Well-connected 5yo who beat a subsequent bumper winner when scoring by just over 7l on Irish point debut in February 2025 (heavy ground); tailed off when reappearing in Exeter maiden hurdle (2m, good to soft) in January but was only 3-1 for that and ought to be capable of considerably better.

stable_tour.quote: A half-brother to Gwennie May Boy, he won a point-to-point for Derek O'Connor. He's a nice, big, good-looking horse who we're looking forward to going over hurdles this season. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Half-brother to useful hurdler Perfect Myth; worth a glance in the betting before debut
runners.spotlight: Third foal; half-brother to useful 2m-2m3f hurdle winner Perfect Myth; dam quite useful 6f/7f Flat winner; entitled to learn from this debut outing but still worth a glance in the betting.

runners.comment: Second in Irish point and good-ground bumper here; leading contender on hurdle debut
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on Irish point debut last April and in good-ground bumper here for new stable in November (winner came fourth in Listed race on next start); had wind op soon afterwards; leading contender on hurdling debut.

stable_tour.quote: His sire is starting to get some nice winners over jumps and this one was bought at the April sales after finishing runner-up in a 3m Irish maiden point-to-point. He'll start off in a bumper and then probably go novice hurdling. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Showed clear promise in both bumpers and on both hurdling starts but needs to improve
runners.spotlight: Showed clear promise in both bumpers and on both hurdling starts, most recently when well-held third at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) three weeks ago; needs to improve to threaten the principals here, though.

runners.comment: Irish point/bumper winner; fair form when placed on both British hurdle starts
runners.spotlight: Irish point/bumper winner who showed fair form when placed on both hurdling starts for Harry Fry, latterly when second at Doncaster (2m, good to soft) last month; another big role to play.

runners.comment: Irish point win last year; struggled to get competitive in any of her three hurdle races
runners.spotlight: Won a good-ground Irish point last spring but has struggled to get competitive on any of her three hurdling starts (2m-2m5f).

runners.comment: Always behind when 50-1 for junior hurdle at Doncaster in November
runners.spotlight: Always behind when 50-1 for junior hurdle at Doncaster (good to soft) in November; can only be watched.

runners.comment: Looked quite promising in all three bumpers but probably best watched on this hurdle debut
runners.spotlight: Flat-bred 4yo who looked quite promising in all three bumpers, albeit remote when third on soft ground last time; probably best watched on this hurdling debut, though.

runners.comment: With a good stable but has not shown much against her own age-group on first two starts
runners.spotlight: With a good stable but has not shown much against own age-group on first two starts (bumper/hurdle) and needs to learn to settle better.

racecards.verdict: Stanners Glen is respected but preference is for KILNEW SUPREME, who made a promising rules debut in a bumper here in November.

racecards.race_name: Welcome Back To Racing Caroline Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Travelled well for a long way on chasing debut; drops back from 2m3f here; interesting
runners.spotlight: Good-ground Irish point winner last spring; 0-5 under rules but travelled well for a long way before weakening into fourth on last month's chasing debut at Wetherby (2m3f, soft) and the reduced emphasis on stamina ought to aid his cause.

runners.comment: Five hurdle wins; well beaten on chase debut but this faster ground will suit much better
runners.spotlight: 5-19 over hurdles, with all wins gained on good/good to firm; well beaten on last month's chasing debut at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) but will be much better suited by today's quicker conditions and may yet have a future over fences.

stable_tour.quote: He's a great little horse but hard to predict. One day he'll race for you and one day he won't. He refused to race at all at Ludlow in November. A few weeks later he won going away at Taunton. He's a character and a joy to have around. 14-01-26

runners.comment: Fell mid-race on recent chase debut but was in decent form over hurdles beforehand
runners.spotlight: Fell mid-race here on chasing debut 18 days ago but twice ran well in today's headgear combination over hurdles last month and, with good ground suitable, has a good chance if able to transfer that form to fences.

quotes.race: JCB Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It wasn't really a surprise, to be honest. I rode Sage Green a few weeks ago at Chepstow and made the running that day, and he ran his race a little bit in the preliminaries and down at the start. I said I wouldn't be too despondent on the bare place he's finished, as he ran a nice race on bad ground. I was delighted they put a hood on him today and they said just change tactics, drop him in, and teach him how to race correctly. I didn't know turning in if we'd be good enough but he's done it quite nicely - James Best, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Dual soft-ground winner in recent weeks and today's conditions may suit even better
runners.spotlight: Not bred for fences but has collected small-field chase wins on soft ground at Plumpton (2m1f) and Fontwell (2m2f) in recent weeks, and may be even better suited by the forecast good ground on this hat-trick attempt.

racecards.verdict: Twice a winner on soft ground in recent weeks, SANITISER might be seen to even better effect on this quicker surface.

prev_owners.owner: Strachan, Corbett, Salwey, Inkin, Griffith, Graham

runners.comment: Three-time chase winner; looked lacklustre when pulled up on last two outings
runners.spotlight: 3-8 over fences, including a win in valuable series final at Cheltenham (3m1f, good) last April; lacklustre when pulled up (albeit on soft ground) on last two outings, though, and can't be supported with much confidence here.

quotes.race: Exertis-Samsung Racing Excellence Award Challenger Series Mares' Chase Final (A Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The family are great stayers. I was quite surprised by how well Minniemum travelled into it. She's won a nice prize with the 30,000GBP GBB bonus. She jumps nicely - Henry Daly, trainer.

quotes.race: Racingtv.com Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: It's just unfortunate, one of those things, and I feel sorry for the owners and the stable staff at home. I thought today Minniemum would lose her maiden tag and everything had gone right, she'd got into a nice rhythm. It's a shame. We'll try again - Richard Patrick, rider.

runners.comment: Place twice on soft ground (3m1f/3m5f) since cheekpieces were added; respected
runners.spotlight: Third in a quite valuable Hereford mares' chase (3m1f, soft; first-time cheekpieces) in December and also ran well when filling same position in Bangor marathon (3m5f, soft) last month; might not be ideally suited by the quicker ground here but still respected.

stable_tour.quote: She was beaten a head on her sole chase start at Exeter in February and I decided then to leave her as a novice over fences for this season. She won over hurdles at Chepstow in April but she looks like a chaser through and through and there are lots of mares' novice chases for her to target, 26-10-23

quotes.race: Abba Party Raceday Saturday 4th May Mares' Open National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 1 Elim') (GBB) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Taxus Baccata pretty much made all in her point-to-point as well and she has a lovely attitude. I did feel like I was tying up in the last furlong but it's tiring ground, I've pressed on a long way out and it was a game performance - Conor O'Farrell, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.owner: Noel Fehily Racing Syndicate & Miss J Wignall

quotes.race: Wincanton Supports The RSA Mares' Handicap Chase (Challenger Mares' Chase Series Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Moviddy has put in a lot of good efforts and very often bumped into one so it's very satisfying to get that chase win. We'll quite possibly have a go at the final in which she finished fourth last year - Noel Williams, trainer.

racecards.verdict: This might be best left to TAXUS BACCATA, who has stamina to prove but is still on a good mark after her recent Leicester win.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Taxus Baccata, 9/4 Lagonda, 3/1 Moviddy, 6/1 Minniemum

racecards.race_name: Jim Morgan And Ronnie Stevens Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Jim Morgan & Ronnie Stevens Memorial Trophy)

runners.comment: Looked out of sorts when pulled up twice for new yard last month
runners.spotlight: Won a big-field Listed handicap at Listowel (2m, good to yielding; first-time cheekpieces) for Willie Mullins in September but looked out of sorts when pulled up twice for new yard last month (no headgear, as today).

quotes.race: Listowel Races Supporters Club Lartigue Hurdle In Memory Of John Molyneaux (Listed Handicap)
quotes.quote: The cheekpieces helped to sharpen up Last Kingdom's jumping and helped him to travel through the race. I felt we were a little bit at sea without them at Galway. I thought they might just help to bring out a bit of improvement, and they did. He jumped much better and travelled sweeter. I committed him plenty early, but I was confident of him staying on that ground, and he did. He saw it out nicely - Paul Townend, jockey.

quotes.race: Farmhouse Foods Novice Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Mark [Walsh, jockey] said Last Kingdom has grown up a little bit since the last day. He said he jumped well and missed the last but still would have managed to win and he travelled away smoothly. He's happy on that ground and he might make into something like a Lartigue horse, he's only four - David Casey, trainer's assistant.

stable_tour.quote: Cheekpieces brought about improvement when he won the Lartigue at Listowel. That was a big step back in the right direction. 17-11-25

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late J P Carrington

runners.comment: Career-best form when winning at Taunton in January; excused recent defeat on heavy ground
runners.spotlight: Showed career-best form when comfortably winning from Bourbali at Taunton (2m3f, good to soft) in January and a subsequent lesser effort on heavy ground there is not viewed harshly; has been ridden by a good 7lb claimer lately, though, and might find others better handicapped.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wasn't sure after Celtic Art's his first run but he's definitely been getting better at home. He coped with this soft ground which is nice, he never runs well on quick ground so maybe this is the answer. He was very green at the backend of the race, so we'll need to get that sorted if he's going to progress. He's a lovely horse - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

quotes.race: Betway Handicap
quotes.quote: Celtic Mill has a big heart and needed it to get past Living Legend - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Matchbook EBF Peter Willett Future Stayers' Maiden Stakes (Plus 10 Race) (Sire/Dam-Restricted Race)
quotes.quote: Celtic Art is a big baby and the ground was way too quick for him. He'll be a lovely horse next year - PJ McDonald, jockey.

runners.owner: W Pope, E Legg, M Green & T Swaffield

quotes.race: "Book Christmas Festival Hospitality Now" Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There might just be improvement to come from Bourbali over a fence. He's obviously very good around here - Joe Tizzard, trainer speaking to RTV.

stable_tour.quote: He's a great, genuine little chap. He carried 12st on Saturday at Wincanton and that's a tough ask as he's not the biggest. He's been put down 1lb, but the handicapper knows exactly where he is. He won't be easy to place, but he'll have his day at some point. 12-11-25

His saddle slipped at Exeter in November. I'm not sure that was trainer fault, but he went and won next time at Kempton so I was forgiven! We then stepped him up in grade for the Wayward Lad and he got into a fight with a superior horse up front, which probably cost him as they went like the clappers. That's how he is and the handicapper has got hold of him, but he's a genuine little horse who runs his race every time. I'll have to pick and choose my way with him, but wouldn't be afraid of running in the better races because there's good prize-money in some of them without winning. He ran a solid race at Wincanton last week and is too consistent for his own good. 18-01-24

He picked up an injury after his first run of last season at Chepstow, which put him on the back foot. He's not always been the most fluent of jumpers over fences, which is why we started him back over hurdles at Aintree, but we're hoping a clear run can help him this season. 18-11-25

runners.owner: O C R Wynne & Mrs S J Wynne
runners.comment: Gave good account when third at Chepstow (2m7f) last month and has each-way claims again
runners.spotlight: Yet to make any significant progress since winning hurdle debut in autumn 2024 but still has fairly low mileage and gave good account when keeping-on third in first-time tongue-tie at Chepstow (2m7f, soft; first run after wind op) last month; should be okay over this shorter trip; each-way claims.

stable_tour.quote: He had a nasty fall at Wincanton last November and his form tailed off after. He had a lovely comeback run at Newton Abbot and I'm much happier with him, so we could go to Cheltenham for Saturday's intermediate handicap hurdle. It won't be long before we go chasing as he schools well over fences. 12-11-25

He's a lovely big baby and his owners are happy to be patient with him this season. He took a big step forward at Wincanton last time and James Tudor said he had a job to pull him up. We'll probably run him in another bumper and then he'll be turned away before coming back as what I hope is a smashing novice hurdler next autumn. 18-01-24

prev_owners.owner: Mrs T Hyde & Mrs T P Hyde & Mrs Paul Shanahan

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse and should have a real good season as a novice hurdler. We bumped into a potentially smart one of Dave Pipe's at Ascot in December, but he showed enough promise in that Listed bumper for us to let him take his chance in the Grade 2 at Aintree, where a staying-on fourth strongly suggested he'll be suited by further over hurdles. 04-11-25

runners.owner: F J Mills & W R Mills
runners.comment: Creditable fourth in good-quality Ascot contest last month; leading claims
runners.spotlight: Not quite in peak form this season but has still made the frame in some good-quality contests, most recently when close fourth of 15 at Ascot (2m3f, good to soft) last month; in calmer waters here and will be suited by the faster ground; leading claims.

quotes.race: Jason Salleh Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Maybe it was because Moveit Like Minnie was in front, but he just ran out. He didn't give me much warning. I was down the inner and he ran out on the outside, so he's gone the whole way across the fence. I felt I had the winner covered, but I'm not going to say I definitely would have won because nobody knows. For the horse to do what he did probably means he had plenty left in the tank - Tom Bellamy, jockey.

quotes.race: RhinoBet Michaelmas Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: We learnt Moveit Like Minnie needs two miles. He was always fading at the last over further and he doesn't anymore. That was brilliant and we are chuffed to bits. He does need better ground and the Betfair Hurdle is usually on softer ground, but we will look at a better handicap now - Nigel Twiston-Davies, trainer.

runners.comment: Back in prime form when scoring at Plumpton this month and now 4-10 over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Back in prime form when scoring in first-time tongue-tie at Plumpton (2m4f, good to soft; front pair clear) a fortnight ago and now 4-10 over hurdles; recent 4lb rise does not look excessive and he should be fine on the faster ground here; likely contender.

quotes.race: Exeter Junior "National Hunt" Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: With three inexperienced horses it turned into a sprint up the straight but he showed a willing attitude in fighting off the second. Valadon is a tall, scopey individual who's more of a galloper and very much in the National Hunt mould - Harry Fry, trainer.

racecards.verdict: The feature can go to class-dropper MOVEIT LIKE MINNIE (nap), who has been very competitive in some strong Ascot handicaps this season.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Moveit Like Minnie, 4/1 Valadon, 9/2 Celtic Art, 5/1 Ambion View,  Swingin Safari, 8/1 Bourbali, 9/1 Crebilly, 25/1 Last Kingdom

racecards.race_name: Golf Membership On Sale Now Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Looked quite promising on seasonal debut but has gone the wrong way since; tongue tied
runners.spotlight: Looked quite promising when fifth in an Exeter novice (2m, good to soft) on seasonal debut in November but has gone the wrong way since; might be aided by new tongue-tie here but has questions to answer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had two good runs and was second behind The New Lion last October. Everything went wrong after that and he'll need a run to get his mark, but he's more than capable of winning races. 12-11-25

prev_owners.owner: G Strawbridge, J Wigan & T Hirosaki

runners.comment: Three wins in early part of this season; player if fully tuned up after four-month break
runners.spotlight: Did well for new stable in early part of season, winning three times (2m2f-3m, good/good to soft); absent since below-par run in the autumn but can play a significant role if fully tuned up.

quotes.race: BetWright All Bun & Games Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It was Christian [Leech, husband] who was adamant Stiletto should go back up in distance. He was able to travel strongly and stay on well. He's a really fun little horse. Hopefully this will kickstart the autumn campaign - Sophie Leech, trainer.

runners.comment: Kept on for third on heavy ground last month; might progress again if today's ground suits
runners.spotlight: Well beaten on handicap debut in January but last month's keeping-on third at Taunton (2m3f, heavy) was much better and further progress is possible if the much faster ground here suits.

runners.owner: Syd Hosie Racing Syndicate - Ribba Hill
runners.comment: Well beaten in first two handicaps but today's better ground can enable improvement
runners.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who showed some hurdling promise on good ground towards the end of last year; well beaten in both subsequent handicaps (good to soft/heavy) but may well fare better now back on a sound surface.

runners.comment: Twice well beaten since a fairly encouraging hurdle debut but remains open to improvement
runners.spotlight: Twice well beaten (1m7f/2m3f) since his fairly encouraging hurdle debut at Exeter (2m, good to soft) in the autumn but has been given a wind op before this handicap debut and remains open to improvement.

runners.comment: Ran well for a long way on handicap debut; can feature if today's faster ground suits
runners.spotlight: Displayed significant promise in two slow-ground maidens here (1m7f) in January and ran much better than eventual 60l defeat suggests on last month's handicap debut at Exeter (2m5f, heavy); not out of this if the much quicker surface suits.

runners.comment: Pulled up when 40-1 for last month's handicap hurdle debut; difficult to enthuse over
runners.spotlight: Became disappointing on the Flat last year and has not shown much since switched to hurdling; pulled up when 40-1 for last month's handicap hurdle debut at Taunton (2m3f, good to soft); difficult to enthuse over.

runners.comment: Ran okay here (3m) in December on his second start after along layoff; not seen since
runners.spotlight: Respectable fourth here (3m, good to soft) in December, his second run after a long layoff, but absent for another 109 days since and current ability remains tricky to gauge.

prev_owners.owner: L J Williams & J D Packer Syndicate

runners.comment: 0-11 over hurdles and absent since pulled up last summer; has had wind operation since
runners.spotlight: 0-11 over hurdles and absent since pulled up in first-time cheekpieces at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good) last summer; needs subsequent wind op to have made a big difference.

runners.comment: Showed no significant promise in three maiden/novice hurdles; handicap debut today
runners.spotlight: Showed no significant promise in three maiden/novice hurdles (1m7f-2m5f, good to soft-heavy) but has a lowly mark and sports first-time cheekpieces for this handicap debut; improvement possible.

runners.comment: Well beaten in all three handicaps; today's better ground offers some hope
runners.spotlight: Well beaten in all three handicaps (2m4f-3m2f, good to soft-heavy); could plausibly be seen in a better light on today's faster ground but it takes a leap of faith to support him.

runners.breeder: S A R L Crispin De Moubray Et Al
runners.comment: 0-5 over hurdles but returned from long absence with an encouraging run this month
runners.spotlight: Unplaced all five hurdle starts but returned from 596-day absence with an encouraging fourth at Taunton (2m3f, good) a fortnight ago and has possibilities if that run brought him on.

racecards.verdict: The suggestion is TOBI KANOBEE, who ran well for a long way on his handicap debut and will hopefully be suited by this faster ground.

runners.comment: Four-time hurdle winner but she's been well held in two Flat runs this month; opposable
runners.spotlight: Four-time hurdle winner but this 7yo has been well held in two Flat runs (1m3f/8.6f) this month, with an RPR of 47 on both occasions; opposable.

quotes.race: Get Best Odds Guaranteed At Unibet Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Laravie is a really nice filly and having the visor equipped to her has helped. That was the best she has jumped today and Sean [Bowen, jockey] gets on really well with her. We did try her in cheekpieces before, but I just think she needed a break when we got her from Ireland more than anything. She will upgrade as she goes up in trip. Unfortunately, there is not any race for her now in the English programme until the winter. We are going to give her a little break and go to either Limerick or Cork in October for a Listed fillies' hurdle race and we will try and get some black type with her. We thought about it the other day that if she won today we would then try and get some black type with her before the winter - James Owen, trainer.

runners.comment: Finished in rear in two runs this year and she remains best watched for now
runners.spotlight: Tailed off on Kempton debut last month and she finished out the back again at a massive price here (9.4f) two weeks ago; she remains best watched for now; stablemate of Estissa.

runners.comment: Made a low-key start at Newcastle in January and she needs to leave that form well behind
runners.spotlight: Weak 16-1 shot and she finished last of five after a slow start at Newcastle (7f) in January; should know more this time but she needs plenty of improvement upped in trip.

runners.comment: Showed promise in Ireland in the autumn and she needs a close look on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Well-bred filly who was a promising fourth at Gowran Park (1m, heavy) in the autumn, on the second of two runs for Ger Lyons; returns after six months off but she's a half-sister to an AW winner and needs a close look for new yard.

runners.comment: Has striking pedigree and she made a promising start at Lingfield in December; key player
runners.spotlight: Dubawi filly who is out of 1m-1m2f winner (including AW/French Group 1/US Grade 1; RPR 119); ran green after a slow start at Lingfield in December but she made some late headway to finish a 4l third of 11; that was a promising start and she should know much more this time; key player.

runners.comment: Makes limited appeal on paper and hood is applied on debut; best watched
runners.spotlight: Third foal; dam 63-race maiden (runner-up 6f/7f; RPR 64), half-sister to winners Cubswin (11.6f Flat/useful 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Inspirited (7f), out of 1m2f winning half-sister to Australian 12.5f Group 2 winner Fantastic Love; hood is applied on debut and she is best watched.

runners.comment: Plenty to like on paper and interesting to see how she figures in the market
runners.spotlight: Third foal; dam unraced sister to useful 7f winner Ametist, half-sister to winners Good Guess (7f Group 1) and Spangled (7f Group 3), is granddaughter of 1,000 Guineas winner Russian Rhythm; plenty to like on paper and interesting to see how she figures in the market.

runners.breeder: Boyce Bloodstock & Mrs C E Percival
runners.comment: Half-sister to eight winners and she needs a close look in the market on debut
runners.spotlight: 55,000gns foal, 68,000gns yearling; half-sister to eight winners including Hors De Combat (7f/1m; RPR 113), Stroll Patrol (6f; 104) and Yourtimeisnow (6f 2yo including Group 3; 102); dam maiden half-sister to US 1m1f Grade 1 winner Stroll; has a striking pedigree and she's an interesting newcomer.

runners.comment: Well held on Leicester debut in September and she needs a transformation on her return
runners.spotlight: Out of a 7f Group 1 winner; always behind and finished a well-held seventh at Leicester (7f, good to soft; 14-1) in September; with a top yard but she's drawn out wide on her return and needs to leave that initial form well behind.

runners.comment: Well held in both her runs and will be more interesting when switched to handicaps
runners.spotlight: Beaten 10l on Newbury debut (7f; 25-1) last summer and it was a similar story on her C&D reappearance last month; still early days but handicaps look the way forward after this.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to ESTISSA who was an eyecatching third on her Lingfield debut in December and should know much more this time.

runners.comment: Win and third over C&D in last two starts and she's respected with cheekpieces added
runners.spotlight: All four wins have been on Tapeta, the latest from a wide draw over C&D last month; ran another solid race when third here ten days ago and she remains feasibly treated on her best form last year; respected with cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: On a dangerous mark but he's finished down the field in last ten starts; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Won a Brighton handicap off 9lb higher last May but he's finished down the field in ten runs since; he wasn't beaten far over C&D ten days ago but overall record is now 3-38 and others are preferred.

quotes.race: Ire-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: It all happened a bit too quickly for Zu Run on his debut at Salisbury over the six furlongs. He missed the break and got unbalanced at times but I felt that he hit the line well enough for an extra furlong to help him and that's exactly what happened here. He showed a good attitude to the line and it's nice that he's taken a good step forward from that first experience - David Probert, jockey.

runners.comment: Fair fifth at Kempton but he still has something to prove at this trip and is 0-10 on AW
runners.spotlight: Well handicapped on his best form last year and he ran into some trouble in the closing stages when a creditable fifth at Kempton (6f) last time; hard to rule out another good run but he still has something to prove at this trip and is 0-10 on AW.

runners.comment: On a workable mark but she's faded in her last three runs and is now 0-17
runners.spotlight: Runner-up with visor added at Newcastle (7f, Tapeta) in her final two runs last year; looks interesting on that form but she's faded in her last three runs and is now 0-17.

quotes.race: Ian Angry Anderson Celebration Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Neptune Legend was very happy out in front. Hopefully he can build on it as he's definitely grown since earlier in the year. He was in control and he's a lovely type, which bodes well for later in his career-Oishin Murphy, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I thought he would need the run last week when making his debut at Nottingham and I was right to a degree, but he still ran a terrific race and had he not run green he could have won. He had a good blow afterwards and I am sure there is an awful lot of improvement to come. We will see how he builds on that run but Plan A at this stage is to win a maiden and then possibly go for the Coventry, but there is a lot of water to pass under the bridge before that. 29-05-21

runners.comment: Disappointing over 6f latest but he was in good form over C&D before that; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Disappointing at Southwell (6f) last time but he went close over C&D on his penultimate run and that was after an emphatic front-running success at this track; drawn out wide on this step back up in trip but has possibilities if he can bounce back.

quotes.race: Bet £10 Get £40 With BetMGM Handicap (Rider Restricted Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't plan to make the running but I've jumped well from [stall] nine and, when you jump that well you don't take back. Faster Bee is a horse we learned at home was struggling to breathe so a tongue-tie was applied. He is a bit timid and I was worried he'd curl up if they came to me like he has done in the past and I'm delighted for his owners - Gina Mangan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Flopped in hat-trick bid here in November but he had wide trip; needs close look on return
runners.spotlight: No win in his first 23 starts but he made the breakthrough at Catterick (6f, soft) in October and followed up with a strong-finishing success over C&D; flopped back at this track in November but he had a wide trip and remains feasibly treated on his penultimate run; needs a close look back from a break.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Handicap
quotes.quote: Blue Jay Way had been showing a lot at home, but we just didn't have the ground he wants and he's a strong-travelling horse. He's the nicest horse I've ever trained. He's a lovable horse; he'll stand there all day and let you cuddle him. We've always known he had potential, but it's just getting it out of him because when it rains, it really rains here and we can't get him out every day - John Riches, trainer.

runners.breeder: Julia Scott, J F Dean & Lady Trenchard
runners.comment: Seven-race maiden who has finished a tailed-off ninth in his four handicaps; opposable
runners.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who has finished a tailed-off ninth in his four handicaps (6f-9.4f) and all of those runs have been on AW; opposable.

runners.comment: Eye-catching third at Chelmsford (6f) last time and has claims back up in trip
runners.spotlight: Seven-time winner including two over C&D; hasn't seen much action since her latest success in September 2024 but she kept on well to snatch third at Chelmsford (6f; first-time blinkers) last month; continues to drop down the weights and has possibilities back up in trip.

runners.comment: Unplaced in all 14 starts; blinkers are now tried and she needs to raise her game
runners.spotlight: Unplaced in all 14 starts and was always in the rear in a classified event at Southwell (7f) last month; blinkers are now tried and she needs to raise her game back in a handicap.

racecards.verdict: The most solid option is FISTRAL BEACH, who was a good third in her bid for a C&D double ten days ago and remains feasibly treated.

runners.comment: Handicap newcomer who is a possible improver back up in trip; needs watching in market
runners.spotlight: Sister to Italian 6f 2yo/7f winner Be The Winner; well held at big prices in three maiden/novice events this year but this is more realistic and she's a possible improver back up in trip on handicap debut; needs watching in the market.

runners.comment: Seven-time turf winner but this veteran is 0-13 on AW; others are more persuasive
runners.spotlight: Seven-time turf winner but he's 0-13 on AW; made some late headway when a respectable third here (9.4f) in December but this veteran has not really fired in his last two runs and others are more persuasive.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't really plan to be that far back, but I couldn't have gone much quicker. Revich clearly thrives on this track and this is his type of ground. He's a little terrier when he's under pressure and I got a really nice lead into it from Jason (Hart, jockey Titan Rock) and he took me to the winning line. I suppose they raced up the inside yesterday and it might be a bit chopped up on that rail. It's drying ground, it's fine - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: CAA Stellar Earl Grosvenor Handicap
quotes.quote: Revich doesn't know how to run a bad race but there's something about coming to Chester. He loves a bend, he likes it when it's soft and he was off his last winning mark so there were a lot of boxes ticked today. You need luck here and they did go plenty hard enough up front, to negate the fact that he didn't quite ping the lids as we'd have hoped. He got the gap at the right time but you still need the horse to go through it and he showed such a tenacious attitude to go through. Jim gave him a great ride, he didn't panic, he kept his head and the horse went through with it. We might look at a 70,000GBP handicap at Newbury next week to run in under a penalty because daylight was second and we may need to do something sharpish - Tim Palin, owner's racing manager.
